conventions.convention: Assume AC for the Radon–Nikodym constructions and their consumers.
Measure domination means inequality on every measurable set; the accepted flow is the greatest measure dominated by both forward and transposed proposal flows.

Choose jointly measurable nonnegative representatives f and g with f+g=1 everywhere; acceptance is min(1,g/f) where f>0 and 1 where f=0. Different choices need agree only almost everywhere under the forward flow and may change transitions from target-null starting states.

The common-density formula assumes a sigma-finite common reference measure and finite-valued nonnegative measurable target and jointly measurable proposal densities. Its acceptance value is 1 on the forward-zero set.
All rejected mass remains at the current state. Reversibility means symmetry of the joint flow; invariance alone supplies no irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence, rate, or CLT conclusion.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For finite positive measures ρ and σ, put λ=ρ+σ and choose nonnegative measurable densities f=dρ/dλ and g=dσ/dλ modified so that f+g=1 everywhere. Then η(A)=∫_A min(f,g) dλ is the greatest measure dominated by both. The measurable function a=min(1,g/f) where f>0 and a=1 where f=0 takes values in [0,1] and is a version of dη/dρ.

Assume AC. Given a standard-Borel space, target probability π, and probability proposal kernel Q, form μ(dx,dy)=π(dx)Q(x,dy), its transpose, and their greatest common submeasure η. Choose the specified jointly measurable [0,1]-valued acceptance version α=dη/dμ, set r(x)=1−∫α(x,y)Q(x,dy), and return P(x,A)=∫1_A(y)α(x,y)Q(x,dy)+1_A(x)r(x).

Assume AC and the hypotheses of alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel. Its output P is a probability kernel, the joint measure J_P(dx,dy)=π(dx)P(x,dy) is symmetric under coordinate swap, and π is invariant for P. No irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence-rate, or central limit theorem conclusion is asserted.

Assume AC. Let λ be a sigma-finite positive measure and ρ,σ finite positive measures absolutely continuous with respect to λ, with finite-valued nonnegative measurable densities f,g. Then η(A)=∫_A min(f,g) dλ is the greatest measure dominated by both ρ and σ.

Assume AC. On a standard-Borel space with sigma-finite reference measure λ, suppose the target has finite-valued nonnegative measurable density p and the proposal has finite-valued nonnegative jointly measurable density q. A jointly measurable version of d(μ∧μᵀ)/dμ is min(1,p(y)q(y,x)/(p(x)q(x,y))) where p(x)q(x,y)>0, and 1 otherwise. The algorithm's chosen version agrees with it μ-almost everywhere.

alerts.finding: ex-abc-vanishing-acceptance, Verification step 2.1, states: “For current x and proposed y both inside the tolerance event ... [F3] accepts with probability one” and concludes “the acceptance probability is 2ε”. The cited alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel permits arbitrary measurable RN representatives and explicitly warns that versions can change transitions from target-null starting states. For 0<ε<1/2, fix x₀ inside the tolerance interval. The vertical set {x₀}×[0,1] is null for both proposal flows and their sum. Modify the algorithm's representatives there to f=0 and g=1, preserving f+g=1 and both RN identities. Its prescribed acceptance is then 1 for every proposal from x₀, including out-of-event proposals. The acceptance probability from this admissible current state is 1 rather than 2ε. The example does not specify a pointwise common-density version or qualify its assertion to almost every current state or stationary initialization.

seams_checked.note: The MH theorem establishes a pointwise probability kernel and symmetric joint flow before invoking the general-state reversibility-implies-invariance theorem. The supplier requires no prior invariance or density assumption.
This is contextual prerequisite ordering. The Gibbs page imports no MH ratio or accepted-flow theorem; its summary preserves the distinction between invariance, reversibility, and convergence.

The HMC theorem treats the deterministic proposal through graph-supported flows, constructs explicit normalized forward/reverse densities, and identifies the energy-ratio acceptance version before applying MH invariance. It does not incorrectly assume a Lebesgue proposal density.

MALA explicitly chooses the common-density acceptance version with positive finite target and Gaussian proposal densities, verifies the standard-Borel and sigma-finite-reference hypotheses, and claims reversibility and invariance only.
PMMH applies MH to the extended target and proposal, retaining the complete auxiliary state on rejection. Its invariance deduction does not infer convergence or mixing from MH.

The ABC algorithm and invariance theorem faithfully use the general accepted-flow construction. However, downstream ex-abc-vanishing-acceptance step 2.1 strengthens the almost-everywhere acceptance identity to a pointwise assertion for current states; the exact null-state counterexample is recorded in alerts.
